name: TreeView (+ GlassTreeView alias)
material_impl: Bespoke CSS module (TreeView.module.css): backdrop-filter blur(var(--aura-glass-neutral-level2-backdrop-blur)) + --aura-color-glass-surface/border/shadow tokens. No shared primitive (not OptimizedGlass/LiquidGlass). Inline container vars hard-code '--tree-view-selected-bg: rgba(255,255,255,0.24)' and ignore the color prop; TREE_COLOR_MAP (7 intents) is computed but never used.
motion: CSS transitions only on box-shadow/transform via aura motion tokens; no reduced-motion media query in the module CSS.
a11y: role=tree and aria-multiselectable on <ul>, but no roving tabindex, no ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End/type-ahead navigation (every TreeItem is tabIndex=0). WAI-ARIA tree pattern is only partly implemented.
api: forwardRef, className/style passthrough, controlled/uncontrolled expandedIds/selectedIds. The declared items prop (data-driven tree) is ignored. showIcons/showLines are no-ops. glassVariant/blurStrength/intent/elevation/tier are declared but not destructured, so they leak onto the <ul> as unknown DOM attributes. Sizes are named small/medium/large while most of the library uses sm/md/lg. GlassTreeView is an identical alias. The root GlassTreeView export points to a different implementation (data-display/GlassTreeView), so the name collides.
fake_complexity: No. It is a plain tree, but the color/items/showLines features are advertised and not implemented.
target: data-display/GlassTreeView (single canonical Tree with full WAI-ARIA keyboard model)
justification: This is the second of three tree implementations, and the root export already ships a different GlassTreeView under the same name. The color prop is dead code, the items prop is ignored, keyboard support stops at Left/Right/Enter, and the material is bespoke CSS rather than the shared glass primitive. Pixel analysis of the certification screenshot shows a small, achromatic list on a white canvas with no visible depth or intent color. Merge the compound API (TreeView/TreeItem children) into the canonical tree, add roving focus, then delete this folder.
evidence: src/components/tree-view/TreeView.tsx:73-89 items/glassVariant/intent not destructured -> spread to <ul> at :221
src/index.ts:484 vs src/components/tree-view/TreeView.tsx:241 GlassTreeView name collision

name: TreeItem (+ GlassTreeItem)
material_impl: TreeItem.module.css: the .glass class uses var(--glass-neutral-level1-surface) + blur(var(--aura-glass-neutral-level1-backdrop-blur)). Label color is hard-coded to rgba(var(--glass-color-black)/.95) !important, and the selected state is also forced black, so it is unreadable on dark themes.
motion: Height animates via CSS transition on a measured scrollHeight plus a perspective rotateX(-5deg) on collapse. useReducedMotion only removes the transition; the rotateX transform still applies. A SpringConfig is computed (finalSpringConfig) and never used. Measured height is captured once per expand, so expanding a nested child does not grow the parent's fixed height and the content is clipped.
a11y: role=treeitem sits on the <li>, but focus goes to the inner div, so the focused element has no role and the treeitem itself is never focused. Collapsed children stay in the DOM at height 0 with tabIndex=0, so keyboard users tab into invisible items. The expand toggle is a div with onClick and aria-hidden: double-click and ArrowRight are the only alternatives. Focus-visible box-shadow ring exists in CSS.
api: forwardRef, className/style. color is applied to a CSS var. animationConfig/motionSensitivity are ignored. Throws outside TreeView.
ssr: 'use client'; useLayoutEffect + requestAnimationFrame produce an SSR warning on the server.
fake_complexity: Partial: it imports a spring-physics config path that does nothing.
justification: This item has several defects: focus lands on a role-less div, hidden children remain tabbable, nested expansion clips because of the fixed measured height, the label is forced to black with !important, and a dead spring config is computed. It is not worth polishing in isolation. Fold the compound child API into the canonical tree.
evidence: src/components/tree-view/TreeItem.tsx:220-237 rotateX applied even when reduced motion
src/components/tree-view/TreeItem.tsx:337-356 role on li, tabIndex on inner div

name: GlassPanel

stories.title_note: filed under Controls/Inputs; Default story overrides background with opaque rgba(255,255,255,0.86); grids use non-existent class glass-glass-grid-cols-*; emoji icons

material_impl: Shared primitive: OptimizedGlassCore with intent/elevation/interactive. This is the correct pattern. Padding maps to glass-p-* classes, except xl which uses the raw Tailwind class 'p-8'.
motion: Inherits from OptimizedGlass; adds 'transition-all duration-200' (Tailwind) without reduced-motion handling.
a11y: Plain div; interactive=true adds no role, tabIndex, or keyboard behavior.
api: forwardRef, className passthrough, variant (default/primary/success/warning/error) maps to intent. The variant name 'error' versus intent 'danger' is inconsistent. The conflicting types.ts GlassPanelProps (title/collapsible/glassVariant) is dead and diverges from the real props.
fake_complexity: No.
duplicates: GlassCard / Glass primitive surfaces across the library
target: Glass/OptimizedGlass surface primitive (expose padding prop there) or canonical GlassCard
justification: This is a thin, correct wrapper around the shared primitive, which makes it one of the healthier files in this shard. Its whole value-add is a padding prop and an error-to-danger rename. Fold padding into the primitive and alias GlassPanel to it. The story masks the material by painting the panel 86% opaque white, so the certification screenshot does not show glass at all.

name: GlassAccordionUI

stories.title_note: story imports data-display/GlassAccordion directly, so the wrapper is never rendered; Variants story passes no items

material_impl: None of its own; it re-exports data-display/GlassAccordion.
motion: Inherited.
a11y: Inherited.
api: React.FC with no forwardRef, so refs break versus the base. It re-exports the base under three names (GlassAccordion, Accordion, GlassAccordionUI). The dead GlassAccordionUIProps in types.ts diverges.
fake_complexity: N/A. It is a pure alias.
justification: This is a 17-line alias that also drops ref forwarding. It inflates the component count and the public API surface with no behavior. Keep a deprecated re-export for one minor version if needed, then delete it.

name: GlassCheckboxUI
material_impl: None; it re-exports input/GlassCheckbox.
motion: Inherited.
a11y: Inherited.
api: The root export 'GlassCheckboxUI' is actually the base Checkbox (src/index.ts:836 exports Checkbox as GlassCheckboxUI), while the local GlassCheckboxUI FC wrapper (no forwardRef) is unused. Confusing triple naming.
fake_complexity: N/A.
justification: This is a pure naming alias. The root already exports GlassCheckbox, so this adds API noise only.

name: FocusIndicator
material_impl: Inline rgba box-shadow/outline built from a hard-coded colorToRgb map (indigo 99,102,241; MUI-like purple/orange/green), not tokens. The glow+glass path adds a hard-coded blur(16px) saturate(1.4).
motion: Uses useMultiSpring, but start() is never called and getTargets() is never invoked. Animated values stay at their initial 0, so the indicator never renders: box-shadow spread 0, outline width 0.
a11y: Broken: visible=true still produces a 0px ring, and it never reacts to :focus/:focus-visible of its children. highContrast yellow is computed for the outline only, and the outline is always 0px.
api: forwardRef. The style prop is hijacked as the focus style enum (solid/dashed/glow), and real CSS goes in componentStyle, which is non-standard. target, width, shape, animated, glassVariant, intent, elevation, tier and blurStrength are declared, unused, and leak to the DOM via ...rest.
fake_complexity: Yes: it advertises spring-physics focus animation and renders nothing.
justification: This is a non-functional component. The spring targets are never applied, so the ring is permanently 0px. The certification run reported 'no issues', which shows the certification does not check behavior. Pixel analysis of the screenshot finds no ring pixels and no chroma anywhere. There are already two other focus-ring implementations. Delete this one and standardize focus on a single token-driven focus-visible ring.

name: RippleButton
material_impl: Wraps GlassButton inside a div that also gets createGlassStyle({neutral, level2, high}), which stacks two glass surfaces (double blur and border). Ripple color comes from a hard-coded RGB map (default white at 0.3 alpha).
motion: CSS keyframe ripple; reduced motion is respected (no ripples). Removal uses setTimeout with no unmount cleanup, which can set state after unmount. Ripples fire on mousedown only, not on keyboard or touch-pointer activation.
a11y: The underlying button keeps its semantics. The ripple is aria-hidden. Ripple feedback is absent for keyboard users. The wrapper div steals className, so consumers cannot style the button itself.
api: The ref goes to the inner button, but className/data-testid go to the wrapper and style goes to the button, which is a split passthrough. rippleSize uses small/medium/large while the button size uses sm/md/lg, and getRippleSize(size) with 'md' falls to the default. rippleDuration is declared and ignored. Odd aria-pressed string coercion.
fake_complexity: No, but the comment claims it 'inherits physics interactions' from the base.
justification: Ripple is a press-feedback option, not a component. GlassButton already contains ripple code, and wrapping it here double-stacks glass and splits prop passthrough. Move a pointer-event-based ripple into GlassButton behind a prop and delete this wrapper.

name: StateIndicator
material_impl: Overlay div with color-mix tints from a hard-coded RGB map plus mix-blend-mode: overlay. With glass=true it spreads createGlassStyle({elev:2}) onto the overlay. The overlay sits at z-index 1 above children.
motion: CSS pulse for loading, gated by reduced motion. OK.
a11y: Purely visual: no role=status, no aria-busy for loading, no aria-disabled for disabled. Communicates state by color only (WCAG 1.4.1). The 'warning' and 'info' states declared in types fall to transparent.
api: forwardRef, className/style. size, animated, glassVariant and blurStrength are declared and leak to the DOM. State naming mixes interaction states (hover/active/focus) with status (success/error).
fake_complexity: Mild: states are advertised but not rendered.
target: data-state attributes + tokenized state layers on the base surface primitive
justification: Painting an overlay with blend modes over arbitrary children is not how a premium system expresses state. State layers belong in each component's token set, keyed by data-state. Half of the declared states render nothing, and there is no assistive-tech exposure.

name: VisualFeedback
material_impl: CSS module keyframes (pulse/glow/highlight/bounce/shake/ripple). The optional glass overlay uses createGlassStyle. Ripple color comes from a hard-coded RGB map.
motion: All effects are infinite CSS loops while active; reduced motion disables the class. Infinite shake/bounce is a usability smell. The ripple setTimeout has no cleanup.
a11y: No semantics. type and message props are declared but never rendered, so the 'feedback' is invisible to assistive tech.
api: forwardRef with manual ref merge. type, message and position are declared, unused, and leak to the DOM (message as an attribute).
fake_complexity: Mild: the message/type/position props suggest a toast-like feedback system that does not exist.
target: motion preset tokens (src/animations) applied via a shared Motion primitive
justification: This is a grab-bag effect wrapper that duplicates motion presets and ripple code elsewhere. Its feedback props (message/type/position) are unimplemented. A premium system exposes named motion tokens, not an infinite-shake div.

name: GlassAdvancedDataViz

tests.note: templated smoke/axe/snapshot test, identical to other generated tests

material_impl: Wraps the Glass primitive, but the chart internals are hand-rolled SVG with a palette that mixes tokens with hard-coded hex (#8B5CF6, #EC4899, #06B6D4, ...), stroke='white' point outlines, and a gray grid. Raw Tailwind classes (flex, px-3, rounded) are mixed with glass-* utilities.
motion: The enableAnimation flag only adds a 'transition-all duration-300' class to the path. No reduced-motion handling.
a11y: The SVG has no role, title, desc or data table alternative. The tooltip is mouse-only, and points and bars are click-only (no keyboard). Export and legend buttons are real buttons (good). The drill-down remove button is a bare '✕' without a label.
api: React.FC, no forwardRef, className only. type supports 'pie' | 'scatter' | 'heatmap' but only line/bar/combo render, so the other types silently render empty axes. enablePan, enableCrosshair and showDataLabels are unused. PNG/SVG export does nothing. Legend toggling is broken: processedData filters out hidden series and the legend maps processedData, so a hidden series disappears from the legend and cannot be re-enabled.
ssr: 'use client'. window.innerWidth is read during render when the tooltip is visible. Static pattern id='grid' collides across instances. onWheel calls preventDefault on React's passive wheel listener, which is ineffective and logs a warning. Hit-testing uses unscaled coordinates while the SVG is CSS-scaled (maxWidth:100%), so the tooltip misfires on narrow screens.
fake_complexity: Yes, moderately: the 'Advanced' features (pie, heatmap, scatter, pan, crosshair, PNG/SVG export) are declared and absent.
justification: This is a fourth chart implementation with a broken legend toggle, half of its declared chart types missing, grid lines drawn on top of the data, and no accessible data alternative. Pixel analysis of the certification screenshot shows a single pale grey line inside a light frame with 0% chromatic pixels, so the hex and token palette does not even resolve to color in the certified run. Fold any useful drill-down/filter/export logic into the canonical chart and delete this file.
evidence: src/components/visualization/GlassAdvancedDataViz.tsx:324,940 legend maps filtered data -> cannot re-show series

name: VoiceGlassControl (+ VoiceGlassDemo alias, GlassVoiceCommands)
material_impl: Bespoke inline voiceSurfaceStyle with hard-coded rgba(255,255,255,.14/.28/.3) plus glass-backdrop-blur-lg classes. Raw Tailwind (bg-blue-500, bg-white/20, w-10 h-6) is used for the toggle switch, and many glass-text-primary-glass-opacity-* class names look invented.
motion: framer-motion. Enter animations are gated by reduced motion, but whileHover scale 1.05 on the main panel is not gated, and the initial opacity:0 states remain under reduced motion because animate={} never resolves them to 1. Under reduced motion, panels can stay invisible.
a11y: The primary mic toggle is an icon-only button with no aria-label. Settings and Help panels have no role=dialog, focus trap or Escape handling. The feedback toggle is a button without role=switch or aria-checked. Status text is not in a live region. Labels are not associated with inputs (no htmlFor).
api: Default-export function component, no forwardRef, no style passthrough, fixed positioning hard-coded. wakeWord defaults to 'Hey Genesis' (a product brand leak).
ssr: 'use client'; window access is inside effects (OK). It overwrites the global speechSynthesis.onvoiceschanged handler twice (hook and component) and nulls it on unmount, clobbering other consumers.
fake_complexity: Yes, completely: SpeechRecognition is never instantiated, isListening/transcript/wakeWordDetected are never set to true or non-empty, and the local setLastCommand only speaks the feedback text without updating state. The only real capability is speechSynthesis TTS. The file header admits it is a DEMO with mock data, yet it is root-exported twice (VoiceGlassControl and VoiceGlassDemo).
target: move to examples/ (non-published) or rebuild on interactive/GlassVoiceInput with a real recognition adapter
justification: This is a mock dressed as a product feature. Recognition is never wired, state setters are never called, and the brand-specific wake word ships in a public library. It is root-exported under two names. Its a11y gaps (unlabeled icon toggle, non-dialog modals) would fail review. Remove it from the published surface.

name: GlassChartsDemo (+ GlassDefs, chartGlass, axisTokens internals)
material_impl: Static inline SVGs with hard-coded hex (#70d6ff, #a78bfa, #34d399) and rgba(226,232,240,.14) gridlines tuned for dark backgrounds. chartGlass tokens assume white-on-dark (var(--glass-white) 88%) text, so they are illegible on light themes. The comments reference Recharts and an 'admin portal' from another codebase.
motion: None. useReducedMotion and ANIMATION are imported and unused.
a11y: SVGs have role=img + aria-label (good) but carry no data.
api: Function component, className/children only.
fake_complexity: Yes: the subtitle says 'Live chart primitives' over hard-coded arrays of static paths.
justification: This is a static marketing illustration published as a root component. The fixed three-column grid does not collapse on mobile, and the colors are hex literals. Recharts helpers copied from another app (GlassDefs/chartGlass) belong in the chart system's theme layer, if anywhere.

name: GlassLinkButton
material_impl: Mostly raw Tailwind (bg-gradient-to-r from-blue-500/80 to-purple-500/80, border-white/20, focus-visible:ring-blue-500/60, h-10 px-4), which consumers without Tailwind JIT scanning node_modules will not get. Two stacked createGlassStyle overlays plus a mask-composite border trick. Hard-coded blue-to-purple gradient: a 2021 'glassmorphism' look, not a token-driven system.
motion: Tailwind transitions and an active translate; no reduced-motion handling.
a11y: Native <a> with a focus-visible ring (Tailwind-dependent). disabled:* classes do nothing on an anchor, so there is no aria-disabled handling. The h-8 small size is under 44px despite the touch-target class.
api: forwardRef, className passthrough. intent is ignored for variant=primary, and the noise prop is unused. Prop naming (variant/intent/size) differs from GlassButton.
fake_complexity: No.
justification: GlassButton already supports asChild, so a separate link button with its own Tailwind-only styling fragments the button family and breaks for non-Tailwind consumers. Replace it with <GlassButton asChild><a/></GlassButton> and remove this file.

name: GlassPrismComparison
material_impl: Bespoke: createGlassStyle in compact mode; elsewhere inline rgba(255,255,255,.24), boxShadow rgba(125,211,252,.6), and gradient text set imperatively via ref callbacks. Many class names look invented or duplicated (glass-gradient-primary repeated 3x in one string, glass-inline-glass-block, glass-via-yellow-400). Text is forced to black via local token overrides and rgb(15,23,42) literals.
motion: Heavy framer-motion: around 20 infinite floating particles, an infinite gradient shift, pulsing text-shadow, a rotating custom cursor, and refraction streaks. Most animations are gated by reduced motion, but the 4.2s auto-rotate setInterval is not. A leftover dead prismStyle object is computed inside the useEffect.
a11y: glass-cursor-none hides the system cursor. Interaction is mouse-only (no keyboard or touch control of the prism). Auto-rotating content has no pause control (WCAG 2.2.2). Category buttons are fine.
api: Takes only HTMLAttributes; content is hard-coded.
ssr: 'use client'; seededRandom for deterministic particles (good); ResizeObserver guarded.
fake_complexity: Yes: it hard-codes AuraOne marketing claims ('10,000x Quantum-accelerated training', '100% Formal verification', 'ISO 26262, DO-178C, FDA Automatic certification') and calls a CSS clip-path divider a 'prism'.
justification: This is a product landing-page section with unverifiable regulatory and performance claims embedded as constants. It does not belong in a design-system package. It is mouse-only, auto-rotating, and hides the cursor. If a 'prism reveal' material effect is wanted, build it as a WipeSlider variant over the real Liquid Glass primitive.

name: GlassWipeSlider (+ ComparisonImage, ComparisonContent, FeatureComparison, MetricsComparison, SLIDER_PRESETS, AURAONE_COMPARISON_EXAMPLES)
material_impl: Bespoke inline rgba gradients for the divider and handle (rgba(255,255,255,.28/.14), rgba(71,85,105,.x) shadows) plus glass-foundation-complete/glass-backdrop-blur-md-medium classes. Template-literal Tailwind classes such as glass-duration-[${...}ms] cannot be generated by any JIT, so they are dead. ComparisonContent's default background is raw Tailwind from-slate-900 via-blue-900.
motion: framer-motion handle with useMotionAwareAnimation (reduced-motion aware). The custom rAF momentum ignores reduced motion. handleTransform (useTransform) is computed and unused, and springX/springY are unused.
a11y: This is the best part. The container is role=slider with aria-valuemin/max/now, a rich keyboard model (arrows, shift/ctrl steps, Home/End, PageUp/Down, 0-5 presets) and SR-only instructions. Gaps: no aria-orientation for vertical, no aria-valuetext, a static id='slider-metrics' that collides across instances, and the focus ring is a pulsing border (animate-pulse) inside the handle.
api: memo only, no forwardRef. Uncontrolled only: initialPosition is read once, so PresetPositionDemo's external buttons cannot move it (a bug, visible in its own Examples). The large prop surface (compact/preview/contained/density all meaning roughly the same thing) indicates patch-on-patch. Exports vendor-specific AURAONE_COMPARISON_EXAMPLES (Scale AI, OpenAI Gym).
ssr: 'use client'; document listeners attach only while dragging (good). React onTouchStart preventDefault on a passive listener triggers a warning.
fake_complexity: Low: the slider works, but 'momentum' and 'snapping' only run when release velocity exceeds 0.1.
duplicates: no canonical compare slider elsewhere (rg found none)
target: media/GlassCompareSlider (controlled value/onValueChange, forwardRef, pointer events, shared LiquidGlass handle)
justification: This is the only real, working before/after slider in the library, with a solid keyboard model, so it is worth keeping as a concept. The implementation needs a rebuild: controlled API, Pointer Events instead of mouse+touch pairs, forwardRef, collapse compact/preview/contained/density into one size prop, remove dead springs and impossible JIT classes, and render the handle and divider with the shared glass primitive. Strip the AuraOne/competitor marketing constants. Pixel analysis of the screenshot shows a near-white field with the faint divider barely distinguishable (min luminance about 233 in the downsample), so it does not currently read as a premium material.

name: GlassWipeSliderExamples (+ AuraOneVsScaleAIComparison, VerticalFeatureComparison, PerformanceMetricsComparison, ImageBeforeAfterComparison, PresetPositionDemo, GlassWipeSliderShowcase)
material_impl: Composition of GlassWipeSlider plus many invented or duplicated class names (glass-gradient-primary x3, glass-h-500px, glass-via-red-glass-opacity-50) and raw Tailwind (bg-blue-500/20, text-blue-300).
motion: Inherits; a framer chip uses an exit animation without AnimatePresence, so the exit never runs.
a11y: Wrapping divs are role=region with labels (fine). Preset buttons do not move the slider because it is uncontrolled.
api: Demo functions; not a component API.
fake_complexity: Yes: 'Real metrics from enterprise customers' over invented numbers; AuraOne vs Scale AI / OpenAI Gym marketing copy; placeholder 'Image Content' SVGs.
justification: This is showcase/marketing content with fabricated customer metrics and competitor naming, living in src/. It is not root-exported but is still compiled and storied. Move any neutral examples into stories and delete it.

name: MotionAwareGlass (+ MotionAwareGlassCard/Button/Input, useMotionAwareGlassStyles)
material_impl: Raw Tailwind and pseudo-classes: 'backdrop-filter' with no blur value, bg-white/5, bg-white/8 (not a default Tailwind step), border-white/15, plus legacy glass-subtle/glass-strong classes. The useMotionAwareGlassStyles variants all return the same background token. No shared primitive.
motion: framer-motion variants from lib/motionPrimitives, keyed on MotionPreferenceContext. Reduced motion is actually wired (good), but every instance renders an sr-only 'Motion reduced for accessibility' string, which screen readers announce repeatedly as noise.
a11y: With asButton it renders a div with role=button and tabIndex. Its onKeyDown overrides any consumer onKeyDown and calls onClick with a KeyboardEvent cast as any. MotionAwareGlassInput is a div, not an input. interactive=true makes non-button cards tabbable with no role.
api: forwardRef. Variant names (base/subtle/strong/card/button/input) conflate component types with surface levels.
fake_complexity: Mild: 'Input' and 'Button' variants are styled divs.
target: Glass primitive + motion preset prop (reduced motion handled centrally)
justification: Motion preference should be a property of the primitive and the motion tokens, not a parallel family of surfaces, buttons and inputs. This file builds fake buttons and inputs from divs, relies on Tailwind classes that are not part of the token system, and emits SR noise in every instance.

name: Icon set (components.tsx: ~160 glyphs, ~220 exports, GlassIcon named registry, *Icon aliases)

tests.note: getByLabelText passes even though the svg is aria-hidden

material_impl: Not glass. 24x24 stroke icons via createGlassIcon, with names and API mirroring lucide-react. Glyphs are hand-approximated: Settings is a sunburst rather than a gear, CommandIcon maps to Search, FolderKanban = Folder, MessageSquare = MessageCircle path, and Snowflake is a 3-line asterisk. Many aliases point to the same glyph.
motion: None (Loader2 has no spin).
a11y: aria-hidden is forced to true unless explicitly overridden, even when the consumer passes aria-label or title, so labeled icons vanish from the accessibility tree. The test checks getByLabelText, which does not account for aria-hidden, so it gives false assurance.
api: forwardRef via factory, size/color/strokeWidth/absoluteStrokeWidth (lucide parity). It is published at subpaths ./icons/* plus root. The named GlassIcon registry falls back silently to Circle for unknown names.
ssr: Pure SVG; no 'use client' needed; tree-shakable per export.
fake_complexity: No, but the glyph quality is not first-party: it is a lucide look-alike drawn by approximation.
duplicates: inline chevron SVGs duplicated in TreeItem.tsx and GlassWipeSlider.tsx
target: first-party icon set (designed on a grid with optical stroke rules) or adopt lucide as a dependency
justification: Removing the third-party dependency was reasonable and the factory API is fine. The glyphs, however, are rough approximations, several are semantically wrong (Settings, Command), and the aria-hidden-by-default override breaks labeled icons. A premium system needs a deliberately drawn icon family with a gallery story and visual regression. Either commission or draw a real set, or depend on lucide and theme it.

name: createGlassIcon (factory)
material_impl: N/A. Stroke SVG with currentColor.
motion: N/A
a11y: Line 59 sets aria-hidden={rest['aria-hidden'] ?? true} after spreading rest. It should default to hidden only when no aria-label, aria-labelledby or title is present, and should add role='img' when labeled.
api: forwardRef, displayName, absoluteStrokeWidth scaling (correct math). Clean.
fake_complexity: No.
justification: This is a small, correct factory and one of the cleaner files in this shard. The one fix needed is labeled-icon semantics (role=img + aria-hidden=false when labeled), plus a test that asserts accessibility-tree exposure.

name: createIcon (re-export shim)
material_impl: N/A
motion: N/A
a11y: N/A
api: Re-exports createGlassIcon. rg finds no importer anywhere in src.
fake_complexity: N/A
justification: This is a dead 6-line shim with no importers.
